findings.issue_text: [BUG] grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext type-asserts d.l.FromContext(ctx).(*log.ConcreteLogger) and silently falls back to d.New() when the assertion fails, discarding all contextual attributes set by ContextualLoggerMiddleware. When infra/log's FromContext returns a non-ConcreteLogger contextual wrapper, every 'Plugin Request Completed' / grafana-data-egress log line loses pluginId, endpoint, dsName, dsUID and uname with no error surfaced — the egress-audit logs that downstream alerting depends on become anonymous.

[BUG] logRequest no longer emits traceID (tracing.TraceIDFromContext call deleted) and does not compensate for it anywhere, since ContextualLoggerMiddleware only adds endpoint/pluginId/dsName/dsUID/uname. Operators correlating a failed plugin request log with its distributed trace lose the traceID field permanently — log-to-trace correlation for plugin egress events regresses to zero.

[ADVISORY] logRequest's grafana-data-egress log now depends entirely on m.logger.FromContext(ctx) recovering attributes from a ctx enriched by a different middleware (ContextualLoggerMiddleware), creating hidden coupling between middleware stack ordering and log content. Anyone reordering CreateMiddlewares in pluginsintegration.go (moving ContextualLoggerMiddleware after LoggerMiddleware, or constructing the stack elsewhere) silently strips pluginId/endpoint/dsName/uname from all egress logs; the old code's removed 'this middleware should live at the top of the stack' comment was the only guard, and the next maintainer gets no compile or test failure.

[ADVISORY] The entirely new ContextualLoggerMiddleware (69 lines of behavior-bearing logic including the conditional attribute assembly in instrumentContext) ships with no test file in this diff. A regression in instrumentContext (e.g., dropping the dsName/dsUID/uname conditionals or the nil-checks on DataSourceInstanceSettings/User) would silently strip identifying fields from every plugin request log, and no test would fail; note also that its stream endpoints (SubscribeStream/PublishStream/RunStream) bypass enrichment while QueryData/CallResource/CheckHealth/CollectMetrics get it, a asymmetry nothing exercises.

[ADVISORY] TestLogger.FromContext ignores the given context and returns a fresh NewTestLogger(), discarding contextual attributes by construction. Tests using TestLogger to verify logging behavior can never assert on FromContext-derived attributes (endpoint/pluginId/dsName), so the attribute-carrying path that production relies on is untestable with the provided fake — the fake hides regressions rather than exposing them.

[BUG] The rewrite of logRequest silently drops the traceID field from 'Plugin Request Completed' egress logs: the removed block `traceID := tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false); if traceID != "" { logParams = append(logParams, "traceID", traceID) }` is not replaced anywhere, and log.WithContextualAttributes in ContextualLoggerMiddleware only carries endpoint/pluginId/dsName/uname. Operators correlating plugin request logs with distributed traces via traceID lose that join key; dashboards/alerts keyed on grafana-data-egress.traceID break silently.

[BUG] grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext type-asserts `d.l.FromContext(ctx).(*log.ConcreteLogger)` and, when the underlying logger is not a *ConcreteLogger, silently returns `d.New()`, discarding all contextual attributes set by ContextualLoggerMiddleware. Any code path where the infra logger resolves to a non-concrete implementation (e.g. test/log wrappers) logs 'Plugin Request Completed' with no endpoint/pluginId/dsName/uname fields, silently reverting to the pre-diff log content.

[ADVISORY] LoggerMiddleware's output now silently depends on ContextualLoggerMiddleware being stacked earlier in the same slice: the middleware itself no longer adds pluginId/endpoint/uname/dsName, so any caller that constructs the middleware chain without ContextualLoggerMiddleware (or after LoggerMiddleware) gets egress logs with none of those fields, with no compile-time or runtime signal. A future reordering or partial chain construction (e.g. in tests, enterprise bundles, or alternate service wiring) drops all plugin/request identity fields from data-egress logs without any error; the coupling is invisible at the construction site.

[ADVISORY] The new middleware is completely untested: the diff renames instrumentation_middleware_test.go to metrics_middleware_test.go (which no longer exercises the contextual-logger behavior removed from MetricsMiddleware) but adds no test file covering ContextualLoggerMiddleware or instrumentContext. The context enrichment that LoggerMiddleware now relies on (endpoint, pluginId, dsName, uname keys and their nil-guards on DataSourceInstanceSettings/User) has zero regression coverage; a dropped key or wrong middleware ordering ships unnoticed and degrades every plugin egress log line.

[ADVISORY] The stream endpoints SubscribeStream, PublishStream, and RunStream pass ctx through untouched, so plugin-side loggers obtained via the new Logger.FromContext never see pluginId/endpoint/user attributes on streaming requests — precisely the long-lived path where a plugin's own logs are most needed for correlation. Plugin developers debugging streaming pipelines lose contextual fields in their own log output while the QueryData path has them, an inconsistency nothing in the diff or docs calls out.

[BUG] logRequest drops the traceID log attribute with no replacement, silently changing the "grafana-data-egress" log schema despite the PR being labeled a chore rename. The removed block `traceID := tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false); if traceID != "" { logParams = append(logParams, "traceID", traceID) }` is deleted and neither ContextualLoggerMiddleware nor the new FromContext path re-adds it; anyone using the traceID field on "Plugin Request Completed" events to correlate plugin requests with traces loses that correlation, and log-based dashboards/alerts keyed on traceID stop matching.

[ADVISORY] The plog.Logger interface gains a new required method FromContext, an exported API break that is not traceable to the PR's stated intent of renaming a middleware. Every out-of-tree or in-tree implementer of plugins/log.Logger (wrappers in tests, custom pretty loggers, plugin-scoped loggers) now fails to compile until they add FromContext; the PR title says "Chore: Renamed" so a reviewer would not expect an interface-breaking change here.

[ADVISORY] TestLogger.FromContext returns a brand-new detached TestLogger instead of the receiver, so log lines emitted via FromContext are recorded on an unreachable object. Tests that inject a TestLogger and assert on Calls/InfoLogs will silently pass with zero assertions when production code calls logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...), because the record is written to the discarded instance returned by `return NewTestLogger()` — middleware tests added alongside this diff get no real verification of the new logging behavior.

[ADVISORY] grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext silently falls back to d.New() when the infra logger's FromContext does not return a *log.ConcreteLogger, discarding all contextual attributes set by ContextualLoggerMiddleware. If the infra FromContext returns any non-ConcreteLogger type, "Plugin Request Completed" logs lose pluginId/endpoint/dsName/dsUID/uname attributes with no error or signal — the log schema change from this PR is applied inconsistently depending on an opaque type assertion that callers cannot control.

[ADVISORY] ContextualLoggerMiddleware leaves the three stream endpoints (SubscribeStream, PublishStream, RunStream) uninstrumented, so the invariant it exists to enforce — plugin and request details on the logger — does not hold for streaming requests. Stream handling code further down the stack that calls logger.FromContext gets a logger missing pluginId/endpoint/dsName/uname, producing inconsistent log output between QueryData/CallResource paths and stream paths; the next contributor adding a log line in RunStream plumbing gets silently attribute-less logs.

[BUG] grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext discards the contextual logger whenever d.l.FromContext returns any type other than *log.ConcreteLogger, falling back to d.New() which carries none of the request's contextual attributes. On any path where the infra logger's FromContext returns a wrapper/default logger rather than a ConcreteLogger, the LoggerMiddleware's 'Plugin Request Completed' log line silently loses pluginId, endpoint, dsName, dsUID, and uname — the exact attributes this refactor moved out of logRequest and into context, so data-egress logs become unusable for per-plugin auditing.

[BUG] TestLogger.FromContext returns a brand-new NewTestLogger() instead of the receiver, so all log output routed through FromContext vanishes into a detached instance. Any test that installs a TestLogger and asserts on its Logs/ErrorLogs/Calls fields will fail silently (zero calls recorded) once production code switches to logger.FromContext(ctx), because the contextual log goes to a throwaway TestLogger no assertion can reach; existing tests relying on captured logs go from asserting behavior to vacuously passing.

[BUG] ContextualLoggerMiddleware adds contextual attributes only to QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth, and CollectMetrics, passing SubscribeStream, PublishStream, and RunStream through untouched, while the moved contextual-attribute code and the old 'should live at the top of the middleware stack' contract covered the same set — but RunStream is long-lived and any logging within it now runs with an attributeless logger. Stream requests logged by any downstream middleware lose pluginId/dsName/uname attribution, producing unattributed plugin log lines exactly on the endpoints (long-running streams) where correlating logs to a plugin instance matters most.

[ADVISORY] The pluginId, endpoint, uname, and traceID log fields were removed from logRequest's logParams and are now only supplied if the LoggerMiddleware's context happens to have been enriched by the separately-registered ContextualLoggerMiddleware, creating a hidden ordering/registration coupling between two middlewares. Any construction site that wires NewLoggerMiddleware without also installing NewContextualLoggerMiddleware above it (only pluginsintegration.go:159-160 wires both in this diff) emits 'Plugin Request Completed' lines with no pluginId, endpoint, or traceID — the observability contract is now enforced by middleware-stack ordering that nothing asserts, and a future reordering silently breaks per-plugin egress auditing.

[ADVISORY] The traceID field was dropped from the 'Plugin Request Completed' log line with no replacement in the diff; nothing in the shown code adds traceID to the contextual logger's output. Operators correlating plugin request logs to distributed traces via the traceID field lose that join key after this change; if ConcreteLogger doesn't auto-inject traceID into contextual logs, every existing dashboard/alert keyed on traceID in grafana-data-egress events breaks.

[ADVISORY] instrumentContext builds the attribute list as untyped []any key/value pairs hand-rolled at each branch instead of a typed structure, duplicating the exact attribute names ('endpoint', 'pluginId', 'dsName', 'dsUID', 'uname') that LoggerMiddleware's consumers must match by string. The next editor renaming or dropping one key in this slice silently blanks that field in all 'Plugin Request Completed' lines with no compile error; the hand-maintained writer (here) and reader (downstream log parsing/dashboards) are parallel enumerations that will drift.

[BUG] The refactor silently removes the traceID attribute (and the explicit pluginId/endpoint/dsName/dsUID/uname attributes) from the 'Plugin Request Completed' / grafana-data-egress log line, and they only reappear if m.logger.FromContext(ctx) resolves to a *log.ConcreteLogger carrying the contextual attributes. Any Grafana deployment where FromContext returns a non-ConcreteLogger (wrapped or fallback logger) loses pluginId, endpoint, dsName, dsUID, uname and traceID from the data-egress log event entirely — consumers of that log line (audit pipelines, log-based alerts, dashboards keyed on traceID) stop matching, and the loss is hidden under a PR titled as a rename.

[BUG] The traceID field, previously extracted via tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false) and appended to logParams, is deleted with no replacement in this diff — neither ContextualLoggerMiddleware nor logRequest re-attaches it. Even in the happy path, the plugin request log no longer carries traceID unless the infra ConcreteLogger happens to inject it, breaking correlation between plugin egress logs and traces for anyone debugging slow/failing datasource requests; a pure-behavior regression shipped under a 'chore: rename' objective.

[ADVISORY] TestLogger.FromContext returns NewTestLogger(), a brand-new fake that discards both the outer fake's recorded calls (Calls/Message/Ctx fields) and the contextual attributes from the request context. Any test asserting on the 'Plugin Request Completed' log via TestLogger now asserts against a logger nobody records into — assertions silently pass vacuously and contextual-attribute coverage is untestable, so regressions in instrumentContext will go undetected.

[ADVISORY] SubscribeStream, PublishStream and RunStream pass through without instrumentContext, while the deleted comment on InstrumentationMiddleware said it 'should live at the top of the middleware stack' to enrich context for all plugin requests — the intent that stream paths share contextual logging is dropped rather than preserved. Streaming plugin requests get no pluginId/dsName/uname contextual attributes, and the next contributor extending LoggerMiddleware to streams will find the logger context empty on those endpoints.

[ADVISORY] The renamed test file still defines TestInstrumentationMiddleware while the type under test is now MetricsMiddleware, and no test anywhere in the diff covers the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware or the new FromContext-based logRequest path. The core behavior change of this PR (contextual attributes flowing into the egress log) ships with zero test coverage, so a regression in instrumentContext or grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext fails silently in production logging.

[ADVISORY] The PR objective stated in its title is 'Renamed instrumentation middleware to metrics middleware', but the diff actually splits logging behavior out of InstrumentationMiddleware into a new ContextualLoggerMiddleware and changes which middleware injects contextual attributes — the objective was broadened without explicit acceptance of the behavioral change. Reviewers and release-note readers treat this as a no-op chore; the behavioral deltas (attribute ownership moved, traceID dropped, FromContext dependency added) bypass the scrutiny a behavior-changing PR would get, and any consumer of the old InstrumentationMiddleware export breaks as a silent public-surface removal.

[BUG] TestLogger.FromContext returns a brand-new NewTestLogger() instead of the receiver, so the injected test logger no longer captures log calls made through FromContext. LoggerMiddleware.logRequest now calls m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...) (logger_middleware.go line 68); any existing logger_middleware test that injects a TestLogger and asserts on its Logs/Calls/ErrorLogs records zero calls — the assertions either fail (if they check Calls>0) or, where they assert absence, pass vacuously, giving false confidence that logging behavior is verified when it no longer is. Checked diff test files: only metrics_middleware_test.go appears; no logger_middleware test update fixes this mock/real-behavior mismatch.

[ADVISORY] NewContextualLoggerMiddleware, a new 69-line middleware that mutates request contexts for four endpoints, ships with zero tests in this diff. Checked the only test file in the diff (clientmiddleware/metrics_middleware_test.go) — it covers MetricsMiddleware only; no test exercises instrumentContext's attribute enrichment (PluginID, DataSourceInstanceSettings, User branches) or any ContextualLoggerMiddleware endpoint. A regression — e.g. dropping dsUID or ordering this middleware after LoggerMiddleware in pluginsintegration.go — silently strips contextual log fields from all plugin request logs with nothing failing.

[ADVISORY] grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext's non-ConcreteLogger fallback branch (return d.New()) is new logic with no test anywhere in the diff. If infra log's FromContext returns a non-ConcreteLogger (e.g. a wrapped/nop logger under test or in packaged builds), the middleware silently loses all contextual attributes and logs degrade to contextless output — an operator-invisible regression no test catches. Checked fake.go and ifaces.go changes: TestLogger's FromContext returns a fresh logger and is unasserted, so this branch is never exercised.

[ADVISORY] The middleware ordering dependency — ContextualLoggerMiddleware must sit above LoggerMiddleware for m.logger.FromContext(ctx) to see any attributes — is enforced only by position in a slice with no test asserting the composed stack's behavior. A future reorder of this slice silently removes pluginId/dsName/uname from every 'Plugin Request Completed' log line while all unit tests (which construct middlewares individually) still pass; whoever reorders it gets no signal. Checked diff: no integration-level test of CreateMiddlewares output was added or updated.

[ADVISORY] The rewritten logRequest drops the traceID field that was previously interpolated into every 'Plugin Request Completed' log line, relying on grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext to re-inject it via the infra logger's context. Operators and support engineers who correlate plugin request logs to distributed traces by the traceID field lose that join key on every plugin request log line if the infra logger does not attach trace IDs from the context attributes set here (this middleware only sets endpoint/pluginId/dsName/dsUID/uname via ContextualLoggerMiddleware, not traceID), making per-request tracing of slow plugin calls significantly harder after deploy.

[ADVISORY] ContextualLoggerMiddleware sets contextual log attributes only for QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth, and CollectMetrics, while SubscribeStream, PublishStream, and RunStream pass through untouched, so the logger used by downstream middleware has no pluginId/endpoint context on stream paths. Any downstream consumer of these contextual attributes (the LoggerMiddleware's FromContext-based line, future middlewares, or plugin SDK loggers reading the context) emits stream-request logs with no plugin identification, and anyone debugging live streaming plugin issues gets unattributed log lines.

[ADVISORY] The reworked logRequest drops the traceID attribute from 'Plugin Request Completed' egress logs entirely, and the replacement contextual-logger path (NewContextualLoggerMiddleware.instrumentContext) never adds traceID to the context. Anyone debugging or auditing plugin data-egress logs (the grafana-data-egress event) loses the trace correlation that tracing.TraceIDFromContext previously provided; log-based dashboards/alerts that join egress logs to traces silently stop matching after this deploy.

[ADVISORY] grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext silently discards all contextual attributes when the underlying logger returned by infra log.FromContext is not a *log.ConcreteLogger, returning d.New() instead. On any logger implementation path where the type assertion fails, LoggerMiddleware's 'Plugin Request Completed' line emits with no endpoint/pluginId/dsName/uname and no error is raised anywhere, so the enrichment regression is invisible to whoever wires a non-ConcreteLogger in.

[ADVISORY] logRequest no longer records pluginId, endpoint, uname, or dsName itself; those attributes now arrive only if the newly introduced ContextualLoggerMiddleware is stacked immediately above LoggerMiddleware in CreateMiddlewares, making the egress log's field set depend on implicit middleware ordering. If LoggerMiddleware is ever constructed standalone (tests, alternate wiring) or the middleware slice order in pluginsintegration.go is shuffled, egress logs silently emit 'status/duration' only — a silent telemetry regression with no runtime error to detect it.

goldens.comment: The ContextualLoggerMiddleware methods (QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth, CollectMetrics) panic when a nil request is received. This occurs because they directly access req.PluginContext (via the instrumentContext function) without first checking if req is nil. This is a regression, as previous middleware layers gracefully handled nil requests.

The traceID is no longer logged for plugin requests. During a refactoring, the tracing import and the logic to extract and add traceID from the context to log parameters were removed from the LoggerMiddleware. The newly introduced ContextualLoggerMiddleware does not add this information, resulting in missing traceID in plugin request logs and impacting debugging and request tracing capabilities.

The `TestLogger.FromContext` method returns a new `TestLogger` instance via `NewTestLogger()` instead of returning the receiver (f). This causes logs to be recorded on an un-referenced instance, leading to broken test assertions that expect logs to be recorded on the original logger.

This fallback would indeed drop any contextual attributes that were attached to `ctx` (e.g., by the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware via `log.WithContextualAttributes`). However, the finding’s claim that infra/log’s `FromContext` returns a non-ConcreteLogger wrapper (and thus that this will happen in practice) is not verifiable from the diff alone; the diff only shows the potentially lossy fallback behavior if the assertion ever fails.

The new code logs via `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`, but within this diff the only newly-added context enrichment is `ContextualLoggerMiddleware.instrumentContext`, which adds `endpoint`, `pluginId`, `dsName/dsUID`, and `uname` via `log.WithContextualAttributes`—not `traceID`. In the same diff, `LoggerMiddleware` stops attaching `pluginId/endpoint/dsName/uname` directly to `logParams` and instead relies on `m.logger.FromContext(ctx)` to pick up attributes injected into `ctx` by the new `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` (`log.WithContextualAttributes`). Therefore, any situation where `d.l.FromContext(ctx)` is not a `*log.ConcreteLogger` will cause the contextual attributes in `ctx` to be dropped and the "Plugin Request Completed" log to miss those fields, which is a behavior regression introduced by this change.

This makes LoggerMiddleware’s structured output implicitly dependent on middleware ordering/availability: if a caller builds a partial or reordered middleware chain without `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` ahead of LoggerMiddleware, the log line will still be emitted but without those identity fields, with no signal in LoggerMiddleware itself. The diff shows this coupling but does not prove an actual broken wiring elsewhere, so it’s a real design/robustness concern rather than a demonstrable defect from the diff alone.

The log call is now `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`, so trace correlation may still exist if the underlying infra logger’s `FromContext` injects trace fields automatically, but that behavior is not shown in this diff. What is verifiable is that the previously guaranteed `traceID` log attribute is no longer explicitly emitted by this middleware and no explicit replacement is added here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext silently discards all contextual attributes when the underlying logger returned by infra log.FromContext is not a *log.ConcreteLogger, returning d.New() instead. On any logger implementation path where the type assertion fails, LoggerMiddleware's 'Plugin Request Completed' line emits with no endpoint/pluginId/dsName/uname and no error is raised anywhere, so the enrichment regression is invisible to whoever wires a non-ConcreteLogger in.

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/plugins/log/logger.go`, `grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext(ctx)` type-asserts `d.l.FromContext(ctx)` to `*log.ConcreteLogger` and, on failure, returns `d.New()` with no use of `ctx`. That fallback path drops any contextual attributes carried in the passed `context.Context`, violating the new `Logger.FromContext(ctx)` contract in `ifaces.go` and causing `LoggerMiddleware` (now calling `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`) to log without the enrichment when the assertion fails, with no error/visibility.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] logRequest no longer records pluginId, endpoint, uname, or dsName itself; those attributes now arrive only if the newly introduced ContextualLoggerMiddleware is stacked immediately above LoggerMiddleware in CreateMiddlewares, making the egress log's field set depend on implicit middleware ordering. If LoggerMiddleware is ever constructed standalone (tests, alternate wiring) or the middleware slice order in pluginsintegration.go is shuffled, egress logs silently emit 'status/duration' only — a silent telemetry regression with no runtime error to detect it.

adjudication.rationale: In `logger_middleware.go`, `logRequest` no longer appends `pluginId`, `endpoint`, `uname`, `dsName`, etc. (those blocks were deleted) and now logs via `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`. The new `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` (added in `contextual_logger_middleware.go`) is what injects those attributes into the `context.Context` via `log.WithContextualAttributes`. In `pluginsintegration.go`, the middlewares are stacked such that `NewContextualLoggerMiddleware()` is inserted before `NewLoggerMiddleware(...)`, so the default wiring will include those fields; however, the field set now depends on having that middleware present and ordered correctly, and `LoggerMiddleware` used elsewhere/standalone would emit only the remaining `logParams` (`status`, `duration`, etc.) with no explicit failure. This is a real, diff-grounded coupling/ordering concern rather than a guaranteed defect in the shown wiring.
